# Test roster for cli/crew — mirrors fixtures/cli-fleet.txt, swapped in via
# CREW_ROSTER so these tests do not drift when the real fleet.roster changes.
#
# The COUNT of entries here is the assertion — derived, never written down, so
# a row can be added without stating a number twice: `crew status` printing
# fewer rows than there are lines here is what #47 (jq killed the command on the
# first existing box) and #48 (box exec drained the roster FIFO after one
# iteration) each looked like from the outside.
# FIRST, and the position is the assertion (#224): a box that has never
# ticked used to kill the whole loop, so every row BELOW it vanished. Behind
# `cli-hired` the truncation would still have left the healthy row printed and
# the fixture would have passed a one-sided fix.
cli-neverticked claude builder
cli-hired      claude  builder
cli-idle       claude  reviewer
cli-suppressed claude  builder
cli-supp-silent claude  builder
cli-supp-working claude  builder
cli-supp-stuck claude  builder
cli-unreachable grok   reviewer
cli-stopped    codex   builder
cli-nothired   grok    reviewer
cli-noauth     kimi    reviewer
cli-absent     claude  triage
cli-disarmed   grok    builder
# The box whose tenant role never converged (#220). LAST, so the bulk verbs
# have to carry on past every healthy box before reaching it — a skip that
# aborted the run would still have hired the rows above and read as a partial
# success.
cli-unconverged kimi   builder
# Converged by a rig too old to write /etc/rig/manifest (rig#61). It must hire
# exactly like any healthy box — the manifest corroborates, it never decides.
cli-premanifest codex  reviewer
